steps: Name the setup: straight line (180°), point (360°), triangle (180°), quadrilateral (360°), or parallel lines.
Parallel lines: alternate and corresponding angles are equal; co-interior angles add to 180°.
Polygons: interior sum = (n − 2) × 180°; each exterior angle of a regular polygon = 360° ÷ n; interior + exterior = 180°.
Add what you know, subtract from the total (or solve the equation), then check it fits.
method_card.title: Finding Missing Angles
method_card.content:
Almost every angle problem shares out a known total. A straight line holds 180°, a point holds 360°, a triangle 180°, a quadrilateral 360°.

For an n-sided polygon the interior angles total \((n-2)\times 180°\); each exterior angle of a regular polygon is \(360°\div n\), and interior + exterior = 180°.
method_card.example:
Find each interior angle of a regular hexagon.

Sum \(= (6-2)\times 180 = 720°\); each \(= 720\div 6 = 120°\).

steps: Reverse the formulas: from an interior angle find the exterior (180 − interior), then \(n = 360 \div \text{exterior}\). From an angle sum, solve \((n-2) \times 180 = \text{sum}\).
Combine several facts in one figure: shared vertices, ratios of interior to exterior, or angle expressions that must add to a known total.
Always finish by checking your angle fits the rule you started from.

steps: Spot the setup: a straight line (angles add to 180°), a point (360°), a triangle (180°) or a quadrilateral (360°).
Parallel lines give equal angles: alternate (Z) and corresponding (F) are equal; co-interior (C) add to 180°. Vertically opposite angles are equal.
Add the angles you know, then subtract from the total to find the missing one.

steps: Interior angle sum of an n-sided polygon = \((n-2) \times 180°\). For a regular polygon, divide that sum by n for each angle.
Exterior angles of any polygon add to 360°, so each exterior angle of a regular polygon = \(360° \div n\), and interior + exterior = 180°.
For angle algebra, add the expressions, set the total to 180° (triangle) or the correct polygon sum, then solve for the letter.
